purpose: Evaluate the completed laboratory prototype against predefined ground truth. Measure attribution accuracy, normal-operation collection completeness, integrity verification, custody completeness, adaptation latency and observed resource change without altering the retained Phase 1 to Phase 5 evidence.

scenarios.purpose: Confirm that both labelled laboratory slices produce the expected normal-operation evidence and receive correct slice attribution.
Replay an unrecognised slice context as a data-only laboratory test and confirm that the attribution logic avoids assigning it to either approved slice.
Confirm that shared gNB, core and resource evidence remains explicitly ambiguous instead of being attributed to an unrelated individual slice.
Confirm that the evidence index retains radio, control-plane, user-plane and resource observations from the shared controlled run.
Confirm that the approved traffic observation produces a separate elevated collection-priority update for each labelled slice and records the timing.

limitations: The evaluation runs in an emulated two-slice laboratory. It does not claim live operator or production behaviour.
The allocation-anomaly case is a data-only evidence replay. It does not transmit rogue radio signals, alter subscriber records or change slice allocation.
Docker before-and-after snapshots describe total laboratory activity during the controlled run. They do not isolate a causal production cost for the forensic logic.

The current proof of concept uses labelled controlled traffic and retained artefacts. Results are reproducible within the recorded configuration and workload, not a general performance guarantee for every 5G deployment.
